title: Open problem on sublinear round complexity
statement_text: For a deterministic distributed algorithm that, given an $n$-vertex graph $G$ and an integer $d\ge\max(3,\mathrm{mad}(G))$, either finds a $(d+1)$-clique in $G$ or a $d$-list-coloring of $G$, it remains interesting to obtain a bound on the round complexity that is sublinear in $n$ regardless of the value of $d$.
context_text: In the LOCAL model of distributed computing, each node of an $n$-vertex graph has a unique identifier in $\{1,\dots,n\}$, knows $n$ (and here its own list of colors, or the integer $d$), and exchanges messages of unbounded size with its neighbors in synchronous rounds, with unbounded local computation; each vertex must output its own color in a proper coloring, and the round complexity is the number of rounds needed (so the output of $v$ depends only on its ball of radius equal to the round complexity, and any problem can be solved in a number of rounds linear in the diameter). A $d$-list-coloring is a proper coloring in which each vertex gets a color from its own list of $d$ colors. The maximum average degree $\mathrm{mad}(G)$ is the maximum of $2|E(H)|/|V(H)|$ over subgraphs $H$ of $G$. The authors' main result is a deterministic distributed algorithm that, given an $n$-vertex graph $G$ and an integer $d\ge\max(3,\mathrm{mad}(G))$, either finds a $(d+1)$-clique or a $d$-list-coloring of $G$ in $O(d^4\log^3 n)$ rounds, and in $O(d^2\log^3 n)$ rounds if every vertex has degree at most $d$. This is optimal in the number of colors, and the $\log n$ dependence cannot be replaced by $o(\log n)$ even for fixed $d$ (Linial: trees cannot be colored with a constant number of colors in $o(\log n)$ rounds); the assumption $d\ge3$ is needed since $n$-vertex paths cannot be 2-colored in $o(n)$ rounds. Using network decompositions, the round complexity can be replaced by $d^3 2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$ (and $d\,2^{O(\sqrt{\log n})}$ for maximum degree at most $d$), but the authors find these bounds not very satisfying (in most applications they have in mind $d$ is a constant).
notes: Stated as an open direction in prose, no labelled environment; PDF source.
paper_title: Distributed coloring in sparse graphs with fewer colors

title: Question on randomized list-coloring round complexity
statement_text: There is a deterministic distributed algorithm of round complexity $O(\Delta^2\log^3 n)$ that, given any $n$-vertex graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta\ge3$ and any assignment $L$ of lists of size $\Delta$ to its vertices, either finds an $L$-list-coloring of $G$ or finds that no such coloring exists. Is it possible to avoid the multiplicative factor polynomial in $\Delta$ in a randomized version of this algorithm?
context_text: In the LOCAL model of distributed computing, each node of an $n$-vertex graph has a unique identifier in $\{1,\dots,n\}$, knows $n$ (and here its own list of colors, or the integer $d$), and exchanges messages of unbounded size with its neighbors in synchronous rounds, with unbounded local computation; each vertex must output its own color in a proper coloring, and the round complexity is the number of rounds needed (so the output of $v$ depends only on its ball of radius equal to the round complexity, and any problem can be solved in a number of rounds linear in the diameter). A $d$-list-coloring is a proper coloring in which each vertex gets a color from its own list of $d$ colors. The maximum average degree $\mathrm{mad}(G)$ is the maximum of $2|E(H)|/|V(H)|$ over subgraphs $H$ of $G$. The authors' main result is a deterministic distributed algorithm that, given an $n$-vertex graph $G$ and an integer $d\ge\max(3,\mathrm{mad}(G))$, either finds a $(d+1)$-clique or a $d$-list-coloring of $G$ in $O(d^4\log^3 n)$ rounds, and in $O(d^2\log^3 n)$ rounds if every vertex has degree at most $d$. As a corollary, the authors obtain a distributed list version of Brooks' theorem: the deterministic $O(\Delta^2\log^3 n)$-round algorithm for $\Delta$-list-coloring graphs of maximum degree $\Delta\ge3$ (or certifying that no coloring exists). Panconesi and Srinivasan gave a deterministic $O(\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\log^3 n)$-round algorithm that $\Delta$-colors every $n$-vertex graph of maximum degree $\Delta\ge3$ other than $K_{\Delta+1}$, and a randomized variant in $O(\log^3 n/\log\Delta)$ rounds, i.e. with no polynomial factor in $\Delta$; it is not clear whether the same can be achieved for the list version. In a section on recent developments, the authors mention that Ghaffari, Hirvonen, Kuhn and Maus later gave, for $d$-coloring non-complete graphs of maximum degree at most $d$, a deterministic algorithm in $O(d^{1/2}\log^2 n)$ rounds and a randomized one in $d^{1/2+o(1)}(\log\log n)^2$ rounds.
notes: Implicit question in prose: "it is not clear whether we can similarly avoid the multiplicative factor polynomial in $\Delta$ in a randomized version of our algorithm"; PDF source.
